citation: Dong, Xin, Wu, et al. (2019). Small Signal Stability Analysis of Multi-Infeed Power Electronic Systems Based on Grid Strength Assessment
problem: Relate small-signal stability of multi-infeed power-electronic systems to grid strength; generalize SCR/CSCR to multi-infeed (gSCR, CgSCR).
method: Analytical SCR-stability relation for single infeed; extension by eigenvalue decomposition (modal decoupling) of the capacity-weighted Kron-reduced network matrix under homogeneous devices; checked by eigenvalue analysis and time-domain simulation.
closest_overlap_with_our_work: Defines gSCR, one of our static baselines; the smallest eigenvalue of the weighted network matrix sets the PLL-band margin.
exact_remaining_gap: Single system-level index at rated conditions with homogeneous GFL devices and no synchronous-machine electromechanical modes; does not compute per-replacement marginal effects, sign changes across portfolios, or line-reinforcement rankings checked against finite interventions.

citation: Zhou, Xin, Wu, et al. (2023). Small-Signal Stability Assessment of Heterogeneous Grid-Following Converter Power Systems Based on Grid Strength Analysis
problem: Assess small-signal stability of heterogeneous multi-GFL systems (different controls/parameters) through grid strength.
method: Proves a heterogeneous multi-GFL system can be characterized by an equivalent homogeneous one, decouples it into subsystems, and estimates stability and margin via gSCR/CgSCR; modal analysis and EMT on two test systems and a practical system.
closest_overlap_with_our_work: Extends gSCR to heterogeneous GFL fleets; estimates the network-strength margin without a full eigenanalysis.
exact_remaining_gap: System-level PLL-band margin only; no SG-to-GFL replacement portfolios, no tracked electromechanical mode, no analysis of the sign of marginal replacement effects, no line ranking validated against finite reinforcements.

citation: Liu, Xin, Wu, et al. (2024). Generalized Operational Short-Circuit Ratio for Grid Strength Assessment in Power Systems With High Renewable Penetration
problem: gSCR/CgSCR fail under actual (non-rated) operating conditions of multi-converter systems; need an operating-condition-aware strength index.
method: Multi-time-scale analysis of PLL-dominated dynamics; transformation into simple subsystems; defines gOSCR and CgOSCR using actual terminal voltages and power outputs; usable with black-box converters; modified IEEE 39-bus and a practical wind-rich system.
closest_overlap_with_our_work: The gSCR line itself concedes that rated-condition strength indices mis-identify stability once the operating point changes. This supports our claim that static indices are context-blind.
exact_remaining_gap: Operating-point-aware but still one system index for the PLL band. It is not an intervention sensitivity (no re-equilibrated derivative with respect to replacements or branch admittances), has no SG electromechanical modes, and has no portfolio-conditioned sign or ranking analysis.

citation: Ma, Xin, Wu, et al. (2024). Assessing Small-Signal Grid Strength of 100% Inverter-Based Power Systems
problem: Existing grid strength methods assume SG voltage support and are invalid for 100% IBR systems with GFL and GFM inverters.
method: Multi-inverter small-signal model; grid-strength index with an analytically derived threshold; analytical expression for the impacts of GFL and GFM inverters on the stability boundary; modified IEEE 39-bus.
closest_overlap_with_our_work: Same 39-bus test bed; shows the GFL/GFM device mix shifts the stability boundary.
exact_remaining_gap: No synchronous machines (100% IBR), so no SG-to-GFL replacement or electromechanical-mode tracking; no per-unit marginal effects or sign reversal across portfolios; no line-ranking evaluation.

citation: Xin, Liu, Chen, et al. (2025). How Many Grid-Forming Converters Do We Need? A Perspective From Small Signal Stability and Power Grid Strength
problem: Which voltage-source behaviour (GFL with voltage control vs GFM) strengthens the grid in small-signal terms, and how many/where GFM units are needed.
method: Small-signal analysis via equivalent power grid strength (gSCR-type); effect of the GFM:GFL capacity ratio on the stability margin; configuration guidelines; high-fidelity simulations.
closest_overlap_with_our_work: Poses a portfolio-design question (how many and where to convert) and answers it through grid strength.
exact_remaining_gap: Treats GFM addition as monotonically strengthening and GFL as not providing effective voltage support. It does not study SG-to-GFL replacements in the 0.1-2 Hz electromechanical band, sign reversal of the same replacement across (nested) portfolios, or how often a fixed ranking fails.

citation: Yang, Huang, Xin, et al. (2021). Placing Grid-Forming Converters to Enhance Small Signal Stability of PLL-Integrated Power Systems
problem: Where to convert PLL-based converters to grid-forming control to best improve PLL-band small-signal stability.
method: Matrix perturbation theory shows GFM placement is equivalent to increasing gSCR. Placement maximizes the smallest eigenvalue of the capacity-weighted Kron-reduced Laplacian with GFM rows/columns deleted (combinatorial). A greedy heuristic recomputes node participation factors on the smallest eigenvalue after each placement. Two-area and modified 39-bus systems.
closest_overlap_with_our_work: Closest to (i)-(ii): subset selection of converter conversions on a 39-bus system, node participation ranking on a Laplacian eigenvalue, and sequential (context-updated) greedy selection; the authors note greedy is not guaranteed optimal.
exact_remaining_gap: Under their homogeneous-PLL, static-Laplacian model with no SG dynamics, Proposition III.4 (interlacing) makes every PLL-to-GFM conversion stabilizing, so sign reversal is impossible by construction. They do not quantify fixed-ranking failure rates across stable contexts and do not use re-equilibrated full-system eigenvalue sensitivities.

citation: Huang, Xin, Dong, et al. (2022). Impacts of Grid Structure on PLL-Synchronization Stability of Converter-Integrated Power Systems
problem: How grid structure affects PLL-synchronization stability of multi-converter systems.
method: Kron reduction to converter nodes; modal decoupling (homogeneous converters, uniform R/L, constant-current loads, infinite bus); smallest eigenvalue of the grounded Kron-reduced Laplacian sets the margin; closed-form sensitivity of that eigenvalue to line susceptance B_ij (effective-resistance form); guidelines on PLL retuning, converter placement, reinforcing weak connections; 39-bus.
closest_overlap_with_our_work: Closest peer-reviewed precursor of (iii): line-level sensitivity used to choose which weak connection to reinforce for converter small-signal margin, on a 39-bus network.
exact_remaining_gap: The sensitivity is of a static network eigenvalue, not the re-equilibrated (implicit-function) total derivative of the full-system rightmost eigenvalue. The model has no SGs or electromechanical modes, and the smallest eigenvalue is stated to be monotone in network connectivity (reinforcement never hurts). Rankings are not scored against finite reinforcements or against alternative static metrics.

citation: Huang, Wang, Wang, et al. (2024). Gain and Phase: Decentralized Stability Conditions for Power Electronics-Dominated Power Systems
problem: Scalable, decentralized small-signal stability conditions for heterogeneous multi-converter systems (GFL, GFM, SG).
method: Combination of small-gain and small-phase theorems comparing each device's dynamics with network dynamics in an open-loop, decentralized way; less conservative than passivity-based conditions.
closest_overlap_with_our_work: Network-based certificates for mixed GFL/GFM/SG systems, the same device classes as our portfolios.
exact_remaining_gap: Sufficient per-device certificates at a given operating point. They give neither the signed marginal effect of a replacement nor its dependence on the rest of the portfolio, and no line ranking against finite interventions.

citation: Wu, Li, Javadi, et al. (2018). Assessing Impact of Renewable Energy Integration on System Strength Using Site-Dependent Short Circuit Ratio
problem: Existing SCR-based strength indices ignore electrical interactions among multiple renewable sites.
method: Site-dependent SCR (SDSCR) derived from the relationship between system strength and voltage stability; IEEE 39-bus case studies.
closest_overlap_with_our_work: Site-dependent (node) strength metric on the IEEE 39-bus system; the kind of static node metric we benchmark against.
exact_remaining_gap: Static voltage-stability index; no small-signal eigenvalue, no replacement portfolios or sign analysis, no line ranking validated against finite reinforcements.

citation: Henderson, Egea-Alvarez, Kneuppel, et al. (2024). Grid Strength Impedance Metric: An Alternative to SCR for Evaluating System Strength in Converter Dominated Systems
problem: SCR does not represent IBR behaviour and only covers the fundamental frequency; need a frequency-dependent strength metric.
method: Grid Strength Impedance Metric computed from network impedances plus MIMO output impedances of GFL/GFM converters across frequency; time-domain validation; mainly short-term voltage stability.
closest_overlap_with_our_work: Explicit critique of SCR; shows location strength depends on which device types (GFL vs GFM) are deployed.
exact_remaining_gap: Location-strength metric, not an eigenvalue sensitivity; no signed marginal effect of SG-to-GFL replacement across portfolios, no electromechanical-mode tracking, no line-reinforcement ranking versus finite interventions.

citation: Lamrani, Prevost, Cardozo, et al. (2025). Frequency-Averaged Grid Impedance Metric for Identifying Weakest Buses in Power Electronics-Dominated Systems
problem: Identify weakest buses (risk of inverter interaction) in PEIR-dominated systems; SCR-derived metrics are inadequate.
method: Frequency Averaged Grid Impedance (FAGI) metric capturing PEIR under various control schemes, compared with ESCR as implemented in RTE's operational tool; 4-VSC system; dynamic simulations used to check each metric's bus ranking.
closest_overlap_with_our_work: Scores bus rankings from static strength metrics against dynamic ground truth and finds ESCR-derived rankings unreliable, which parallels our static-metric baseline comparison.
exact_remaining_gap: Small 4-VSC system and bus ranking only. No SGs, no replacement portfolios or sign reversal, no line-reinforcement ranking. The fixed-ranking issue shown concerns ESCR-vs-dynamics disagreement, not ranking failure across portfolio contexts.

citation: Yu, Xu, Sun, et al. (2024). Multiple Renewable Short-Circuit Ratio for Assessing Weak System Strength with Inverter-Based Resources
venue: CSEE Journal of Power and Energy Systems 10(6):2271-2282
problem: Identify weak-system status with widely distributed, low-capacity IBRs.
method: Multiple renewable SCR (MRSCR) and its voltage-based critical value (CMRSCR) from a single-infeed equivalent with multiple renewables, linking strength to voltage fluctuation under power variation; implemented in Chinese engineering software.
closest_overlap_with_our_work: Utility-grade SCR-family weakness index; the class of static metric our results challenge for small-signal decisions.
exact_remaining_gap: Static voltage-based index. It does not address small-signal eigenvalues, portfolio-conditioned sign of replacement effects, or line ranking against finite reinforcements.

citation: Zhu, Gu, Li, et al. (2022). Participation Analysis in Impedance Models: The Grey-Box Approach for Power System Stability
problem: Root-cause tracing of small-signal instability without full disclosure of IBR internal models.
method: Impedance participation factor defined as the residue of the whole-system admittance matrix and proved equal to the eigenvalue sensitivity with respect to apparatus impedance; chain rule to state and parameter participation; three-layer grey-box approach.
closest_overlap_with_our_work: Apparatus-level eigenvalue sensitivity as a criticality measure; conceptual parent of node-level eigenvalue-sensitivity rankings.
exact_remaining_gap: First-order local sensitivity at a fixed operating point and portfolio (apparatus impedances not re-equilibrated). It does not study discrete SG-to-GFL replacements, sign changes of their effect across portfolios, or whether any fixed ranking selects the best next replacement.

citation: Zhu, Gu, Li, et al. (2023). Impedance-Based Root-Cause Analysis: Comparative Study of Impedance Models and Calculation of Eigenvalue Sensitivity
problem: Complete theory of impedance-based root-cause analysis, including sensitivities to series-connected (branch) components missing from whole-system participation factors.
method: Formal relations between nodal-admittance (critical admittance-eigenvalue sensitivity) and whole-system impedance models; eigenvalue sensitivity to components and parameters including series elements; three-node network, modified IEEE 14-bus, NETS-NYPS 68-bus.
closest_overlap_with_our_work: Closest peer-reviewed work to (iii): eigenvalue sensitivity with respect to network branch elements for tuning IBR-rich systems.
exact_remaining_gap: The abstract describes no re-solution of the power-flow equilibrium when a branch changes (apparatus impedance models appear held fixed). Line rankings are not validated against finite reinforcements or compared with static metrics (|P| flow, SCR/gSCR, Fiedler, effective resistance), and there is no portfolio conditioning.

citation: Ebrahimzadeh, Blaabjerg, Wang, et al. (2018). Bus Participation Factor Analysis for Harmonic Instability in Power Electronics Based Power Systems
problem: Locate which converters and buses are most sensitive to and contribute most to harmonic instability.
method: System cast as MIMO dynamic admittance matrix; bus participation factors from oscillatory-mode sensitivity to elements of the MIMO transfer matrix; PSCAD simulations of a 400-MW wind farm.
closest_overlap_with_our_work: Node/bus criticality defined via mode sensitivity for converter-driven oscillations.
exact_remaining_gap: Harmonic (high-frequency) instability inside a wind farm, not 0.1-2 Hz electromechanical modes; no replacement portfolios, sign reversal, or line ranking vs finite interventions.

citation: Markovic, Stanojev, Aristidou, et al. (2021). Understanding Small-Signal Stability of Low-Inertia Systems
problem: Stability properties of low-inertia systems with SGs, GFM and GFL converters; maximum permissible IBR penetration.
method: High-fidelity full-order model incl. line and load dynamics; modal analysis, participation factors, parameter sensitivity; nature of unstable modes; directions for improving margins under different generation portfolios on several benchmark systems.
closest_overlap_with_our_work: Replaces SGs with converter-based generation across generation portfolios and uses participation factors to find vulnerable segments; closest system-level precursor to (i).
exact_remaining_gap: Per the abstract, results are organized by penetration level and portfolio type. It does not report sign reversal of the same unit's replacement across (nested) stable portfolios on a tracked electromechanical mode, oracle fixed-ranking failure rates, or line-reinforcement ranking.

citation: Song, Hill, Liu (2018). Network-Based Analysis of Small-Disturbance Angle Stability of Power Systems
venue: IEEE Transactions on Control of Network Systems 5(3):901-912
problem: Role of network topology in small-disturbance angle stability; mechanism of instability.
method: Active power flow graph whose Laplacian weights depend on operating angles (negative weights = critical lines); inertia of that Laplacian determines stability/type of equilibrium; necessary-and-sufficient criterion via critical-line matrix; equivalent weight ('electrical antagonism') as stability index.
closest_overlap_with_our_work: Operating-point-dependent graph Laplacian in which a line's contribution can change sign (critical lines). This is the structural analogue of the contextual sign reversal we find.
exact_remaining_gap: Classical SG swing-equation model with no converters or GFL; the sign change is of an edge weight with operating angle, not of a generator replacement's marginal effect across portfolios. No ranking validation against finite interventions.

citation: Schafer, Pesch, Manik, et al. (2022). Understanding Braess' Paradox in power grids
problem: Adding lines or increasing line capacity can reduce grid performance (Braess' paradox) in realistic grids.
method: Experimental AC grid demonstration plus a topological (flow/cycle-based) theory predicting Braessian edges from network structure; implications for grid-extension planning.
closest_overlap_with_our_work: Shows the sign of a link reinforcement's effect depends on the network/flow context, which motivates scoring finite reinforcements rather than assuming monotone benefit.
exact_remaining_gap: Steady-state line loading, not small-signal eigenvalues or IBR/GFL dynamics; no generator replacement portfolios, no eigenvalue-sensitivity ranking or static-metric comparison for small-signal stability.

citation: Joswig-Jones, Dong, Tan, et al. (2026). Sensitivity-Based System Strength Assessment: Mapping Power Flow and Network Topology Perturbations to System Eigenvalues
venue: arXiv preprint (submitted to IEEE Transactions on Power Systems); arXiv only
problem: System strength assessment without repeated eigenvalue evaluations; identify injections, voltage changes, or line changes that may trigger instability in IBR-rich grids.
method: Closed-form eigenvalue sensitivities (impedance/residue form) to power injections, voltages and line admittances, including power-flow Jacobian terms (chain rule through the operating point); sensitivity indices rank weak buses and critical lines; modified IEEE 14-bus (20 devices) and 118-bus (GFL, GFM, SGs); time-domain checks.
closest_overlap_with_our_work: Closest overall to (iii): operating-point-aware (re-equilibrated) eigenvalue sensitivity to line admittance, used to rank lines and buses in IBR systems.
exact_remaining_gap: Preprint only. Validation uses selected time-domain cases, with no rank correlation of sensitivity rankings against finite interventions. Comparison with static metrics is qualitative (vs impedance margin ratio only, not |P|, SCR/gSCR, Fiedler, effective resistance). Sensitivities change between dispatch cases, but portfolio conditioning, SG-to-GFL replacement and sign reversal are not studied.

citation: Bacic, Niehues, Bottcher, et al. (2026). A graph theoretic view on small signal stability of inverter-based power grids
problem: Necessary and sufficient small-signal stability conditions for lossless inverter-based grids and decentralized certificates.
method: Stability shown equivalent to positive definiteness of a single matrix combining topology, operating point (voltages, angle differences) and droop gains; augmented cone graphs; decentralized criteria and their conservatism; IEEE 9-, 30-, 118-bus.
closest_overlap_with_our_work: Graph-spectral small-signal condition with operating-point-dependent edge weights (topic 11).
exact_remaining_gap: Droop-controlled grid-forming inverters only, lossless, and negative edge weights excluded (cos(theta_ij)>0). No GFL/SG, no replacement portfolios, no sign reversal, no line ranking vs finite interventions.

citation: Ma, Xin, Li, et al. (2023). Characterizing the Role of Complex Power in Small-Signal Synchronization Stability of Multi-Converter Power Systems
venue: arXiv preprint (v2 2024-02-14); arXiv only - no peer-reviewed version found in Crossref
problem: Characterize how each converter's active/reactive power affects PLL-band small-signal synchronization stability in multi-converter systems.
method: Stability indicator quantifying the margin across operating conditions; the 'resultant force' of complex power on the margin expressed as a weighted sum; separate active/reactive effects; cancellation between active power generation and consumption; simulation validation.
closest_overlap_with_our_work: Operating-point (injection) dependence of each converter's contribution to the network-strength margin, decomposed additively.
exact_remaining_gap: Preprint. GFL/PLL band only with no SGs. The additive weighted form implies a fixed-sign contribution per injection type, the opposite of contextual sign reversal. No replacement portfolios or line ranking.

citation: Gu, Green (2023). Power System Stability With a High Penetration of Inverter-Based Resources
problem: How IBR dynamics fit or break classical stability categories; GFL vs GFM synchronization, inertia and voltage strength.
method: Review and analysis; GFL/GFM duality and generalized angle dynamics; discussion of system strength and GFM placement; research agenda.
closest_overlap_with_our_work: Calls for spatial-temporal indices of system strength and stability margin to guide where new stability services go. Our portfolio-conditioned indices address this agenda item.
exact_remaining_gap: Review. No quantitative portfolio-conditioned marginal analysis, no sign-reversal evidence, no ranking evaluation against finite interventions.
